Commentary.Commentary: Having chased down a bigger total in the previous game, the hosts will back themselves to gun this down. However, should the low bounce continue to occur and the Kiwi bowlers hit the right lengths, this target might just look a bit more threatening. Attacking the new balls would be the key as Guptill showed earlier on. Join us back at 1745 IST (1215 GMT) for the run chase.

India struggled with the new balls today. Umesh Yadav and Dhawal Kulkarni went for aplenty in the first 10 and struggled towards the end as well. Hardik was inconsistent but the spinners covered it up for them. New Zealand will be hoping that the pitch continues to stay low and dew does not affect them much.

As has been happening through the series, the Black Caps are guilty of throwing away a set platform. The last 10 overs yielded just 61/3, of which, 40 came in the final 5. It was a difficult pitch to bat on, with the ball staying low on many occasions due to the cracks. Guptill survived a couple of chances en route an entertaining 72 while the rest struggled to time the ball.

Excellent comeback from India again after going for plenty at the start. The Kiwis were 80/0 at the end of 10 overs, which means that they have scored at around 4.5 runs per over in the remaining 40. Spinners were the key again, as the trio of Mishra, Patel and Jadhav went for just 107 in 28 overs, picking up 3 wickets amongst themselves.

Game time! MARTIN GUPTILL and TOM LATHAM come out to bat for New Zealand. India begin with UMESH YADAV! Here we go...
The players are out in the middle for the national anthems.
New Zealand XI -  Martin Guptill, Tom Latham, Kane Williamson(c), Ross Taylor, Jimmy Neesham, Anton Devcich, BJ Watling(wk), Mitchell Santner, Tim Southee, Trent Boult, Ish Sodhi.
India XI - Rohit Sharma, Ajinkya Rahane, Virat Kohli, MS Dhoni (wk/c), Manish Pandey, Kedar Jadhav, Axar Patel, Hardik Pandya, Amit Mishra, Dhawal Kulkarni, Umesh Yadav.

MS Dhoni begins by saying that they were anyways looking to bowl first with the chance of dew later on. Calls it a fantastic performance from the bowlers so far. Acknowledges that batting at Number 4 gives him the chance to get himself in and pick the big shots at  the right time. Says that he is happy to be playing at home but it is all same once the game begins.

Kane Williamson is delighted that he has finally won a toss. Says that they are hoping the pitch slows up and hence are playing 3 spinners. Mentions that they need to stitch together partnerships to stay in the game. He reckons that it is hard to say what is a safe total on board.

TOSS - At last, after what seems an eternity, New Zealand have won a toss on this tour! Kane Williamson wants to bat first. Plenty of changes for New Zealand, Ish Sodhi, Anton Devcich, BJ Watling are in for Matt Henry, Luke Ronchi and Corey Anderson. For India, Jasprit Bumrah is not 100 percent and is out for Dhawal Kulkarni.

The visitors on the other hand, will hope to stay alive in the series with a win. They have got starts but have failed to capitalize on them. Will the middle order finally step up for them? Let's see.

Hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of the 4th ODI between India and New Zealand from JSCA International Stadium Complex, Ranchi. The hosts are leading the 5-match ODI series 2-1 and will be wanting to seal the series today itself with another clinical performance.
